digest.component_or_area: rebar-implement skill and shared test-design documentation
propositions: Five escape classes in implement-side skill and test-design lack coverage: parity siblings at build time, config read-but-miswired behaviors, op-level contention semantics, gate findings without oracle upgrades, and residual gaps at close.
Config keys that change behavior must be validated through real read paths via default vs non-default contrast tests, not merely parsing validation.

Changes composing multiple locked operations, check-then-act patterns, or introducing caches over store state must route contention test cases to existing shared suites by shape rather than define bespoke harnesses.
Behavioral gate findings require a RED test written first in the same change before the fix is applied; non-behavioral findings may be fixed directly.
All out-of-scope slots from the parity census, exclusions, compromises, and deferred advisories must be enumerated and dispositioned as filed, accepted-with-reason, or fixed.
